patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of the apparent cost change is tied to shifts in authorization coding distribution rather than a clear utilization or reimbursement signal. This appears in TX and again in UNATTRIBUTED / VA, so the first business step is to confirm how authorization status is being mapped onto claims before changing policy, contracting, or UM operations.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If this is a coding or mapping shift, acting on it as true medical cost trend would misdirect UM and reimbursement decisions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have UM operations and data quality jointly validate authorization-to-claim mapping and category assignment for the affected periods, then reroute confirmed residual changes to reimbursement or UM teams.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The spend movement is explicitly flagged as an auth or mapping shift requiring validation before business action, and the pattern includes unattributed activity.
evidence_summary: TX authorization coding distribution accounts for about $33.5M of apparent paid change.
UNATTRIBUTED / VA adds another $4.5M of apparent change under the same authorization distribution issue.
Affected examples include kidney and urinary infection DRGs in TX and acute myocardial infarction with MCC in UNATTRIBUTED / VA.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend is the clearest real cost trend in the analysis and is driven first by more admissions, with some added pressure from higher paid and allowed per admit. The signal is concentrated in authorization-required acute hospital claims, so the most likely lever is inpatient utilization management rather than broad product repricing alone.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest actionable medical cost increase in the analysis after removing validation-only noise.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a TX DSNP HMO inpatient management workup focused on admission growth, authorization effectiveness, and recurrent urinary infection stays in acute hospitals.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose $34.7M, driven by 1,628 more admissions and 1,920 more claims.
In the main TX acute hospital signal, average paid per admit rose about $441 and average allowed per admit about $544.
A related TX DSNP HMO acute hospital cluster added another $1.0M, including 45 more urinary infection admissions and paid per admit up about $11.5K on with-MCC cases.

patterns_data.pattern_details: IN / OH has a distinct rare-case pattern driven by a handful of very high-cost admissions, not by broad utilization growth. These include transplant, tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation, cardiothoracic, and other one-case severe events at ASCENSION ST VINCENT HOSPITAL and UHCMC.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These cases can materially move trend despite very low volume, so they need case-level management rather than population-level policy changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform case-level clinical and financial review for transplant, tracheostomy, and other catastrophic admissions, including carve-out, stop-loss, and contract terms where applicable.
evidence_summary: A single heart transplant or heart assist system admission at ASCENSION ST VINCENT HOSPITAL added about $420K.
A single tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation admission at UHCMC added about $401K.
Other one-case cardiothoracic, sepsis, and O.R. procedure admissions added about $0.3M more.
